title: Copy-on-write: after Process 1 writes C
purpose: Show Process1 taking a private copy of C while A/B remain shared and Process2 keeps original C.
requiredChecks: Physical memory has exactly A,B,C,and C′ (private copy) boxes.
Both processes still map A→A and B→B.
Process1 C maps only to C′ and Process2 C maps only to original C.
The write is by Process1, and labels distinguish original C from the private copy without implying Process2 sees the write.
alt: After Process 1 writes page C: A and B remain shared, Process 1 uses a private copy, and Process 2 retains the original C
prompt: Create a NEW original English technical blog diagram. White background, crisp dark navy large sans-serif labels, flat blue/teal outlined shapes, generous whitespace, simple unambiguous connectors, no decorative art, no logos or watermark. TITLE "Copy-on-write: after Process 1 writes C". Three separate well-spaced columns: left "Process 1 — virtual pages" A,B,C; center "Physical memory" four rows A,B,"C — original","C′ — private copy"; right "Process 2 — virtual pages" A,B,C. Both processes' A arrows map to physical A and B arrows map to physical B. Process 2's C maps only to "C — original". Process 1's C maps ONLY to "C′ — private copy", using an elbow connector in the left gap to the fourth physical row. Exactly SIX mapping arrows pointing into physical memory. There is NO remaining Process1→originalC arrow and NO Process2→privatecopy arrow. Highlight the private copy in teal. Put a small note under Process1 "Write to C triggers a copy". Footer exactly "A and B stay shared; only C is copied". All arrow endpoints must be correct and readable; no connectors cross labels.
